name: george-mason-biology
refs_note: the folder of refs/ that holds the reference views (views.json, masks/), which refine, compare, metrics, sky_mask and the viewer's ?sv= read: refs/photos (gitignored), whose views tools/photo_camera.py writes. Its one photograph is taken from the street south-east of the building, square to its south-east end; the copy the project has is squeezed across (1398 x 953): the pilasters 3.5 m apart and the end wall's 13.1 m in the LiDAR give the same scale both ways only with its width stretched 1.2117 times, to 16:9, so the reference is that stretched copy. Its camera is fitted to the end wall (its foot, its top and its north-east corner, its two pilasters) and the attic's top behind it, the only pick off the wall's plane, the camera held near 1.6 m over the LiDAR's ground (rms 1.39 px): a lens of about 109 degrees across whose principal point lies off the picture to the left (a level picture cut from a wider one: its verticals are upright), about 14.6 m from the end wall and 24 m south-west of its middle. Plane trees and a hazy sky: the sky mask finds almost none (2,523 px), so the silhouette IoU tells little; the model laid over the photograph through the fitted camera is the check

building.title: George Mason Biology Building (106), University of Auckland
building.note: outline: traced from the LiDAR (building.outline_note), in the map's frame; chooses the crop box and the building's own points (frame.near_outline, measure and topview). campus_outline: building 106's outer ring from the main project's campus.json, kept for the record; the site replaces block 106 by its id, and topview measures the share of that block under the model.
building.outline_note: traced from the LiDAR's roofs and walls in the view frame of frame.expected: the long block (the south-east end at x 29.1, the north-west end at x -29.4, its long walls at z -6.0 and 6.0), the middle (x -17.0 to 17.0, z -8.8 to 8.8), the two wings to the south-west (to z 12.0), the tower and the strip on the north-east side and the low parts round the foot, taken to the map's frame. campus.json's ring (campus_outline) is about 5 m short at each end (x 25.7 to -25.9) and narrower on the south-west (to z 8.4): within 1.5 m of it the first data run left out the ends of the long block and the wings. frame.expected is the frame measured on campus_outline, kept, so that the model, the camera and the placement keep it.

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north
